findings.current: Michael Silbert did not miss the opportunity to seize the attention of the entire world.
findings.defect: The source says Silbert did not miss the moment when the world’s attention was focused on the event. This wording instead says he seized the world’s attention.
findings.rationale: The Korean describes the timing of Silbert’s opportunity, not an act of attracting the world’s attention.
findings.replacement: Michael Silbert did not miss the moment when the attention of the entire world was fixed on the event.

findings.current: In the grainy footage, the figure called themself the Prophet and pointed to the two heads placed in front of them before continuing.
findings.defect: The English omits the dim lighting and the figure’s robe pulled deeply over their head.
findings.rationale: Both physical details appear in the source and were preserved in the accepted baseline.
findings.replacement: Beneath dim lighting stood an unidentified figure with a robe pulled deeply over their head. In the grainy footage, the figure called themself the Prophet and pointed to the two heads placed in front of them before continuing.

findings.current: Today’s horrific tragedy was only the beginning.
findings.defect: The source includes the audience’s stunned reaction to the Prophet’s threat of judgment before saying today’s tragedy was only the beginning.
findings.rationale: “심판이라니” is an explicit reaction to the announced judgment, not merely a repetition of the following thought.
findings.replacement: Judgment, they said. Today’s horrific tragedy was only the beginning.

findings.current: A lone figure standing in a desert filled with blood and corpses suddenly raised their head.
findings.defect: The English omits that it was a dark night and even the moonlight was dim.
findings.rationale: The source’s setting detail was present in the accepted baseline and is absent from the assembled copy.
findings.replacement: On a dark night, with even the moonlight dim, a lone figure standing in a desert filled with blood and corpses suddenly raised their head.

findings.current: The front page was filled with nothing but openly condemnatory articles and sensational headlines, while fierce battles between netizens raged beneath them.
findings.defect: The English omits the Skeleton King’s observation that even a brief look showed the online news pages were a complete mess.
findings.rationale: This observation appears in the source and the accepted baseline, but not in the assembled English.
findings.replacement: Even from the brief glance he had taken, the state of the online news pages was a complete mess. The front page was filled with nothing but openly condemnatory articles and sensational headlines, while fierce battles between netizens raged beneath them.

findings.current: At least for now, there was no way to reveal the truth.
findings.defect: The English omits the Skeleton King’s realization that his thought was pointless.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly states that he knew the thought was futile; the accepted baseline preserves that beat.
findings.replacement: But the Skeleton King knew it was all a pointless thought. At least for now, there was no way to reveal the truth.

summary: The chapter is mostly faithful, but it drops several source details and slightly changes the focus of Michael Silbert’s action.
